name: Strom Thurmond
role: South Carolina governor (1947–1951) and U.S. senator (1954–2003, with a brief interruption in 1956)
summary: Thurmond ran for president in 1948 on a states’ rights and segregationist platform. In the Senate he opposed the landmark civil rights legislation of the 1950s and 1960s, then backed the 1982 Voting Rights Act extension. His later Senate record included support for NATO enlargement, federal capital punishment and a constitutional balanced-budget requirement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His case for maintaining U.S. strategic superiority called for strengthening U.S. military forces to counter the Soviet Union.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: His vote for the Defense of Marriage Act maintained a federal legal definition of marriage covering opposite-sex couples.

abortion-legal.rationale: Thurmond voted for S.J.Res. 3 in 1983 to overturn Roe v. Wade, and in 1999 voted against the amendment endorsing Roe and for a ban on a specified abortion procedure (98th Senate roll 169 and 106th rolls 337 and 340).

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He voted in 1986 for the military construction bill provisions supplying $100 million in aid to the Nicaraguan Contras (99th Senate roll 610).

civil-marriage.rationale: He voted for the Defense of Marriage Act, which defined the civil status of marriage for federal law as a legal union of a man and a woman.

collective-defense.rationale: He voted to extend the NATO treaty and its Article 5 collective-defense commitment to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic (105th Senate roll 415).

conscription.rationale: He backed moving forward with funding to restore draft registration in 1980 and voted to preserve the denial of federal educational aid to students who did not register in 1983 (96th Senate roll 684 and 98th roll 189).

constitutional-jury-trial.rationale: He supported amendments guaranteeing jury trials in criminal contempt proceedings in the 1957 and 1964 civil rights bills (85th Senate roll 73 and 88th roll 291).

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Thurmond opposed federal voting-rights protections in 1965 but supported their renewal in 1982 and backed the federal holiday honoring Martin Luther King Jr.

death-penalty.rationale: He supported passage of the federal capital sentencing bill S. 1765 in 1984 and voted for S. 1798 in 1989 to authorize the death penalty for terrorist murder of U.S. nationals overseas.

decide-locally.rationale: In his 1948 acceptance speech Thurmond argued that domestic powers should be exercised by state or local governments unless the Constitution delegated them to the federal government.

defeat-communism.rationale: In a 1962 address in Midland, Thurmond urged the United States to abandon what he called a no-win Cold War policy and condemned passively waiting for the communist movement to moderate or fragment.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He voted against direct popular election of the president in 1956 and against final passage of S.J.Res. 26, the 1979 constitutional amendment to replace the Electoral College.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: In his 1948 motion to the Southern Governors’ Conference, Thurmond defended laws maintaining what he called the racial integrity and purity of both Black and white populations.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He voted for West Germany’s admission to NATO in 1955 and for the admission of Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic in 1998 (84th Senate roll 27 and 105th roll 415).

equal-conscription.rationale: He voted in 1972 to preserve laws exempting women from the draft and in 1980 against requiring women to register for Selective Service (92nd Senate roll 524 and 96th roll 690).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Thurmond voted against the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965, then backed the 1982 extension of the latter’s protections against racially discriminatory voting rules.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He voted against delaying additional federal coal leasing in 1983 and backed cloture on the 2002 amendment to allow development in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (98th Senate roll 138 and 107th roll 451).

expand-nuclear.rationale: He introduced S. 919 in 2001 to have the Energy Department assess existing federal sites for construction of commercial nuclear power plants.

farm-price-support.rationale: He voted against removing price supports for millable wheat in 1956 and for freezing farm supports at 1957 levels in 1958 (84th Senate roll 104 and 85th roll 141).

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He voted for the constitutional balanced-budget amendment on final passage in 1995 and again backed it in 1996 (104th Senate rolls 98 and 771).

force-without-un.rationale: He supported authorization to use military force against Iraq in 2002 and opposed an alternative that would have required a new UN Security Council resolution (107th Senate rolls 615 and 617).

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: In his letter on strategic superiority, he endorsed deterring a Soviet attack with a diverse U.S. nuclear arsenal under American control.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: His letter on strategic superiority advocated maintaining a varied U.S. nuclear arsenal to deter the nuclear-armed Soviet Union.

military-superiority.rationale: In his letter on strategic superiority, Thurmond defended a U.S. advantage over the Soviet Union in the quality and quantity of strategic weapons and opposed accepting parity.

more-religion-public.rationale: He voted for constitutional amendments allowing organized prayer in public schools in 1966 and 1984 (89th Senate roll 451 and 98th roll 405).

night-watchman-state.rationale: He voted for an amendment to create price supports for hogs and beef and federal health coverage against catastrophic expenses for Medicare beneficiaries (84th Senate roll 103 and 100th roll 590).

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: His case for retaining U.S. strategic nuclear superiority defended multiple delivery systems, including land-based intercontinental missiles.

patriotic-education.rationale: In his 2002 remarks on the Newdow ruling he called for its reversal so generations of public school pupils could continue learning the Pledge of Allegiance.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He introduced S. 812 to establish a national heritage corridor and support preservation and interpretation of historic places and cultural landscapes in South Carolina.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: He voted for the final Helms–Burton bill, which provided for U.S. support of a transition to a democratically elected government in Cuba (104th Senate rolls 494 and 635).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Thurmond led the Senate campaign against federal desegregation and voted against H.R. 7152 in 1964, which prohibited segregation in public accommodations. His later support for voting-rights renewal addressed electoral access.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He voted for the 1996 Defense of Marriage Act, which restricted federal recognition to opposite-sex marriages and allowed states to withhold recognition from same-sex marriages performed elsewhere.

separate-church-state.rationale: He voted for constitutional amendments permitting prayer in public schools in 1966 and 1984 (89th Senate roll 451 and 98th roll 405).

smash-state-machine.rationale: His 1948 nomination speech called for preserving the existing U.S. constitutional system and restoring the state and local powers he identified with its original design.

state-laws-apply-online.rationale: He voted for an amendment to prohibit Internet gambling and for requiring online sellers to inform buyers about applicable state and local sales or use taxes (105th Senate rolls 527 and 598).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He voted for two constitutional amendments permitting public school prayer and for S. 2690, which reaffirmed the reference to God in the Pledge of Allegiance (107th Senate roll 546).

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: During the Cold War he voted to bring West Germany into NATO (84th Senate roll 27), extending the U.S. commitment to the Western alliance.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He voted for final passage of the USA PATRIOT Act in 2001, which enlarged federal surveillance authority for counterterrorism investigations (107th Senate roll 313).

tax-inheritance.rationale: He opposed retaining the estate tax even for estates above $100 million in 2001 and voted in 2002 to make the repeal permanent (107th Senate rolls 135 and 408).

term-limits.rationale: He voted to advance S.J.Res. 21 and supported instructions for a constitutional amendment limiting representatives to six years and senators to twelve years in office (104th Senate rolls 692 and 727).

total-state.rationale: In his presidential nomination speech Thurmond explicitly rejected a totalitarian state and defended constitutional restraints on government control of elections, policing and private employment.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He supported the 1996 welfare overhaul that established work requirements for cash assistance. In 1992 and 1993 he voted against amendments discouraging general assistance to able-bodied adults outside workfare programs.

notes: Research covered the Senate roll calls, the floor record, his 1948 campaign and gubernatorial statements, and accounts of his legislative record. Topics checked included taxation and labor, constitutional structure and elections, race and religion, civil liberties and criminal justice, military alliances and intervention, energy and the environment, technology, political methods, and international economic policy. The second review focused on class politics, nationalism, segregation, and political violence.
